About

About DappGo

DappGo publishes daily market research for individual investors and builds the apps that deliver it.

What we publish

Every trading day DappGo produces three research reports: one on US stocks, one on Taiwan stocks and one on US options. Each report measures the same things in the same way every session, including market regime, breadth, sector moves, momentum and, for options, the premiums on offer and their risks. The reports are free to read in our apps and on the web.

  • US Stocks, TW Stocks and Options Explorer on iOS, Android and the web.
  • The daily report archive on this site: one readable page per session for each market.
  • DappGo News: headlines for the companies we track, each linked to its publisher.
  • Guides that explain how to read the reports and how every figure is computed.

We also make Number RPG, a mobile game that has nothing to do with markets.

How we work

The reports are produced by software. Data is collected from exchanges, company filings and market-data providers, indicators and labels are computed by fixed rules, and each finished report is published as a single data file with a hash that identifies it. Our apps and this site only display a report whose data matches its published hash. The rules are written down in how DappGo computes its signals.

Some text in the apps is written by language models under strict limits. Where that happens, and where it does not, is set out in how we use AI.

What we are not

DappGo is a publisher. We are not a broker, an investment adviser or a fund, we do not execute trades, and we do not know anything about your finances. Everything we publish is research and educational material. It is not advice to buy or sell anything.

Standards and contact

Our editorial policy covers sourcing, time stamps, corrections, advertising and independence. To report an error or ask a question, see the contact page.

DappGo publishes research and educational material only. Nothing on this page is investment advice, a recommendation, or an offer to buy or sell any security. Prices can be delayed and may contain errors; check them against your broker or the exchange before acting. Past results do not predict future results.
